title: Hurricane Harvey Medical Relief Mission
description: RESIDENTS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS RECENTLY EXPERIENCED DEVASTATION AND MAJOR FLOODING DUE TO HURRICANE HARVEY.  MEMBERS FROM ALL OVER AIR MOBILITY COMMAND WENT INTO ACTION WORKING TOGETHER TO HELP PROVIDE RELIEF FOR ILL EVACUEES. (U.S. Air Force/Staff Sergeant Miquel Jordan)
keywords: Air Mobility Command, HADR, Little Rock AFB, AMC, Pope Army Airfield, Joint Base San Antonio, JBCHS, 628ABWPA, #437AW, 59MDW, #16AS, Hurricane Harvey, Kelly Field Annex, 43AES, 433AES, AIr Force, Texas, C-17, Arkansas, South Carolina, Charleston, Houston, Little Rock

transcript.text: - [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] Members of Joint Base
Charleston assisted in a medical relief mission to aid
those affected by the category four Hurricane Harvey.
- Already packed and ready to go.
We're going to show up, we're going to make sure we have
all the mission planning done like airfield reviews.
Making sure the weather checks any notice as
the airmen go on.
Basically all the normal pilot stuff that we would do,
we're just doing it on a slightly condensed timeline.
- [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] The crew stopped at both
Pope Air Field in North Carolina, and Kelly Airfield
in San Antonio, Texas to collect supplies and medical
personnel in route to Little Rock Air Force Base.
- We're prepping to assign to three teams down to help
with the air patient transport, evacuation, just relief.
We have a lot of medical equipment that we're sending down.
So, help get people out and help transport patients.
- [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] Before loading up, Pope's 43rd
Aerial Medical Evacuation Squadron prepared three full kits
of medical supplies and transport equipment.
After including the equipment from Joint Base San Antonio,
the crews cargo totaled over 15,700 pounds.
- [Female Crew Member] Printing different things.
- You know, I'd been blessed to have the assistance of
Charleston and use and services of the large C-17s here.
But basically what this affords us an opportunity to do
is there, a medical evacuation, medics and nurses is to be
able to transform a large cargo plane like this into a
working hospital so that we can both move sick patients
and family members to the definitive care that they need.
- [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] Upon arriving at Little Rock
Air Force Base, the medical groups were assisted by
the 19th Logistics Readiness Squadron to unload all cargo.
- We were postured to receive the aircraft.
Once they got here, we were here to help download,
and to get everything staged where they needed it to be
staged for to support the local agencies
and State Department.
- [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] The joint effort between
all the bases involved are creating a medical family
for evacuees in need of medical attention due to the
aftermath of Hurricane Harvey.
- [Staff Sgt. Raquel Jordan] Reporting from Little Rock
Air Force base, I'm Staff Sergeant Raquel Jordan.
